column2: Gram-positive cocci in clusters in hospital pneumonia mean S. aureus: patchy consolidation with cavities and pneumatoceles (film a); cover MRSA.
PND with a right effusion in IHD is LVF: film b shows cardiomegaly, upper-lobe diversion and interstitial oedema.
Chronic cough and sweats in a migrant with upper-zone signs is post-primary TB: film c shows bilateral upper-lobe fibronodular shadowing.
Long-standing hypertension with a displaced apex gives the rounded enlarged LV contour of film d; ECG and echo confirm LVH.
PE causes hypoxaemia with hyperventilation: respiratory alkalosis (pH 7.50, PaCO2 3.7) with low PaO2.
Chronic hypercapnic COPD with cor pulmonale: low PaO2, high PaCO2, near-normal pH from renal compensation.
Opioid overdose causes acute hypoventilation: pH 7.06, PaCO2 12.7, PaO2 4.8 on air. Ventilate and give naloxone.
High-flow oxygen in a CO2 retainer causes acute-on-chronic acidosis with high PaCO2 but adequate PaO2; target 88–92%.
DKA: severe metabolic acidosis with Kussmaul breathing, so PaCO2 is very low (1.7 kPa) and PaO2 high-normal.
Recurrent suppurative chest infections with malabsorption in a young non-smoker is cystic fibrosis; sweat test.
Upper-zone nodules with eggshell hilar node calcification after silica exposure is silicosis (raises TB risk).
Bilateral upper-lobe cavitation with sweats, weight loss and haemoptysis in a migrant is post-primary TB; isolate and send sputum.
A solitary spiculated nodule with haemoptysis and weight loss in a heavy smoker is primary lung cancer until proven otherwise.
Lower-zone fibrosis with clubbing and calcified pleural plaques in a plumber is asbestosis.
A child who cannot coordinate an MDI should use it through a spacer before treatment is stepped up.
Exercise-induced symptoms in otherwise controlled asthma: salbutamol shortly before exercise.
Reliever use most days or night waking means uncontrolled asthma: add a regular inhaled corticosteroid (or ICS–formoterol).
Uncontrolled on high-dose ICS + LABA + theophylline: lowest-dose maintenance prednisolone and specialist referral for biologics.
Uncontrolled on low-dose ICS: add a LABA (salmeterol) in a combination inhaler (or switch to MART).
Chronic breathlessness in a smoker with secretions and oedema suggests COPD: spirometry (FEV1/FVC < 0.7) with full lung function tests.
Dry cough, Velcro crackles and clubbing suggest ILD (IPF); HRCT is the key investigation.
Bronchospasm after propranolol with SpO2 < 92%: ABG to detect a normal/rising PaCO2 (life-threatening asthma).
A chest X-ray confirms pneumonia; confusion and hypotension give CURB-65 ≥ 2, so admit for IV antibiotics.
Haemoptysis, hoarseness and hypercalcaemia in a smoker suggest advanced lung cancer: contrast CT chest and upper abdomen first.
Lifelong purulent sputum after whooping cough with clubbing is bronchiectasis; HRCT confirms.
ARDS complicating pancreatitis is graded by PaO2/FiO2 on PEEP, so an ABG is needed.
Stridor from a goitre is extrathoracic obstruction: a flattened inspiratory limb on the flow–volume loop.
Sudden breathlessness and hypotension after hip replacement with a clear chest is PE: CTPA (bedside echo if unstable).
Cavitating bronchopneumonia after influenza is classically S. aureus; flucloxacillin (or MRSA cover).
Headache, fever, dry cough and arthralgia after buying parrots is psittacosis (Chlamydia psittaci); doxycycline.
Dry cough and exertional desaturation in untreated HIV is Pneumocystis pneumonia; high-dose co-trimoxazole ± steroids.
Dry cough, headache, rash and cold-agglutinin anaemia is Mycoplasma pneumonia; macrolide or doxycycline.
Multilobar pneumonia with hyponatraemia, lymphopenia and haematuria in an air-conditioning technician is Legionella; urinary antigen.
Multiple rheumatoid nodules in a dust-exposed worker with RA is Caplan's syndrome.
Calcified diaphragmatic plaques with lower-zone reticulation in a shipyard worker is asbestosis.
A triangular retrocardiac opacity obscuring the right hemidiaphragm (heart border preserved) is right lower lobe collapse.
Dextrocardia with bronchiectasis, sinusitis and infertility is Kartagener's syndrome (primary ciliary dyskinesia).
BHL with dry cough in a young African–Caribbean adult is pulmonary sarcoidosis.
Tramline and ring shadows are the plain-film signs of bronchiectasis, universal in CF.
A lobulated pleural mass with pleural calcification in a dockyard worker is mesothelioma; pleural biopsy.
Gross clubbing with fine end-inspiratory crackles and ground-glass/reticular shadowing is IPF.
More than six anterior ribs above flat diaphragms indicate hyperinflation, as in emphysema.
Persistent hypercapnic acidosis (pH 7.26, PaCO2 9.0) despite treatment in COPD: non-invasive ventilation.
Wheeze and angio-oedema after peanuts is anaphylaxis: IM adrenaline 0.5 mg and high-flow oxygen.
Respiratory distress after trauma with mediastinal shift away from the right is right tension pneumothorax: needle decompression.
A stable suspected spontaneous pneumothorax needs a chest X-ray to confirm and size it before deciding management.
Large traumatic haemothorax: large-bore chest drain (> 1500 mL initially or 200 mL/h means thoracotomy).
Low-severity CAP managed at home: oral amoxicillin (macrolide or doxycycline if allergic).
Late-onset severe hospital-acquired pneumonia needs antipseudomonal cover, e.g. IV ceftazidime or piperacillin–tazobactam.
Severe CAP: IV beta-lactam plus macrolide (e.g. cefuroxime plus erythromycin) to cover atypicals.
Pneumocystis pneumonia: high-dose co-trimoxazole (IV if moderate–severe) with steroids if PaO2 < 9.3 kPa.
Chlamydial pneumonia is intracellular: treat with a tetracycline (doxycycline) or macrolide, not beta-lactams.
Haemoptysis with a monophonic wheeze and SIADH suggests small cell lung cancer.
Recurrent chest infections, failure to thrive and coarse crackles in a child suggest cystic fibrosis; sweat test.
Progressive chest-wall pain with a blood-stained effusion in a builder is mesothelioma; pleural biopsy.
Holly-leaf plaques crossing lobar boundaries in an asymptomatic tradesman are calcified pleural plaques (asbestos exposure); benign.
Six months of nocturnal cough and intermittent wheeze in a well teenager is asthma; confirm objectively.
Haemoptysis, weight loss and sweats with apical consolidation is post-primary TB; isolate and send 3 sputum samples.
BHL with dry cough and breathlessness is most often sarcoidosis.
Clubbing, Velcro crackles and lower-zone reticulation is IPF; HRCT UIP pattern, antifibrotics.
Upper-zone reticulation in a pigeon keeper without clubbing is chronic extrinsic allergic alveolitis; avoid antigen.
A mass within a cavity with recurrent massive haemoptysis is an aspergilloma; Aspergillus IgG, embolise or resect.
Increased purulent sputum and breathlessness on a background of COPD is an infective exacerbation: bronchodilators, prednisolone, antibiotic.
A sucking chest wound with central trachea is an open (non-tension) pneumothorax: three-sided dressing, then drain away from the wound.
Fever, pleuritic pain and bronchial breathing at one base is pneumonia; assess with CURB-65.
Sudden pleuritic pain and breathlessness with a normal chest examination is PE until proven otherwise.
Hyper-resonance, absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation away and shock is tension pneumothorax: decompress without waiting for X-ray.
Suspected cystic fibrosis is diagnosed by the sweat test (chloride > 60 mmol/L) with CFTR genotyping.
Suspected COPD is confirmed by lung function tests (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.7).
Suspected reactivation TB: three sputum samples for AFB smear, culture (with sensitivities) and NAAT.
Haemoptysis, weight loss and a lung mass: staging CT then bronchoscopy and biopsy.
Blood-stained effusion with negative cytology after asbestos exposure: pleural biopsy (image-guided or thoracoscopic).
Acute pleuritic pain and breathlessness: chest X-ray first to exclude pneumothorax, consolidation and effusion.
High-probability PE with contrast allergy and a clear CXR: V/Q scan.
Suspected PE with an abnormal CXR: CTPA, as V/Q would be indeterminate.
Confirmed lobar consolidation explains the pain: sputum (and blood) culture to identify the organism.
Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis: no investigation, immediate needle decompression.
CAP in penicillin allergy: erythromycin/clarithromycin or doxycycline.
Aspiration pneumonia with foul sputum: amoxicillin plus metronidazole (or co-amoxiclav) for anaerobic cover.
Subacute cough with exertional desaturation and perihilar shadowing in HIV is PCP: co-trimoxazole.
